subject: knight
reasoning:
I'm planning out a three.js module to construct an armored knight from basic primitives—standing at roughly 1.8m tall, facing forward, with a helmet and visor, plume, pauldrons, breastplate, tassets, greaves, sabatons, sword, shield, and cape, all sharing a standard material.

Mapping out body proportions and parts...

Positioning the helmet, visor, crest plume, shield on the left arm with an emblem, and a sword in the right hand with blade, crossguard, grip, and pommel.

For the cape, I'll add a wide plane behind the shoulders down to the knees in deep red with a slight flare and tilt. Then I'll add decorative gold trim like a torus gorget and studs, plus a heraldic tabard with a gold cross over the breastplate.

Skipping canvas textures to keep things simple and reliable in a worker context, I'll build a small helper function for adding geometry with position, rotation, and scale, and use deterministic loops for rivets instead of randomness. Now I'm defining the materials and group structure for the knight model...

Working out leg segment positions...

Simplifying to absolute coordinates for the legs instead of relative offsets, then moving to shoulder and arm placement — shoulders at the sides, upper arms hanging down to the elbow, with the right arm angled slightly forward for sword-holding.

Now I'm working out the rotation math for tilting the forearm forward so the hand reaches naturally, figuring out which sign of rotation around the X-axis pushes the limb toward +Z. I'm setting up a helper function that builds a limb mesh from two endpoint vectors and a radius, so each bone segment can be placed consistently.

Using that approach, I'm positioning the shoulder, elbow, and wrist points for both arms, with the right hand gripping the sword and the left forearm holding the shield. For the shield itself, I'm sketching a heater-shield shape using a custom path with curved bottom edges and extruding it to give it some depth.

Now I'm figuring out shield orientation by rotating it around the y-axis so its face points outward, then adding a gold cross emblem. For the sword, I'm working out that it should be planted point-down, with the grip near the hand, guard just below, and the blade extending down to a tip touching the ground, built from simple box geometry.

I'm writing helper functions for cylinder "bars" and box "plates" oriented between two points using quaternions, which I'll use to build limbs and blade segments. Then I'm laying out the torso armor piece by piece—a fauld skirt, breastplate, and a raised ridge detail—using scaled cylinders and boxes to approximate the armored shape.

Now I'm positioning the tabard with its gold cross emblem, tassets hanging from the fauld at specific offsets, and starting on a torus gorget for the neck armor.

Moving to pauldrons as hemispheric domes at the shoulders with rim trim and layered bands, then working down the arms with steel vambraces, couter joints at the elbows, and gauntlet hands gripping the weapon and shield. I'm now sketching out the great helm as a cylindrical bucket shape for the head.

Working out the plume as a backward-curving arc of tapered ellipsoids on the helm's crest, with a visor box, eye slit, and small breath holes for detail. Setting up the neck cylinder and gorget torus to connect head to torso.

Planning the cape as a flared cloth plane hanging from the shoulders down past the knees, positioned behind the body. Building out the thighs, knees, greaves, and sabaton boots for the legs, plus adding gold rivets along the armor edges for detail.

Figuring out the sword geometry -- computing a tilted blade axis from tip to guard, then positioning the grip and pommel along that same direction, with a perpendicular guard box oriented via quaternion rotation.

Now I'm defining helper functions: one to orient a mesh between two points using quaternions, one to build tapered limb cylinders, and simple wrappers for spheres and boxes, which I'll use throughout the rest of the body construction.

Working through the arm positions for both the sword arm and shield arm, placing hands at the grip and at the shield's back face, then shaping the shield itself with a cross emblem on its front.

Refining the plume's arc positions and scale growth, then finalizing the helmet's cylinder-and-dome shape with a visor, eye slit, breathing holes, a gold band, and a small crest ridge on top.

Checking that the pauldrons, breastplate, and neck gorget all align in size and position, then layering in the hip fauld, chest plates, pectoral bulges, and a cloth tabard with a gold cross emblem across the front, extending down as a skirt past the fauld.

Still working out tasset placement...

Confirming the hip-to-thigh leg attachment aligns with the fauld's radius, then moving to write the full implementation.

Writing component metadata and material definitions...

Still writing styles...

Writing the sword geometry functions...

Writing cape mesh code...

Finalizing leg and sabaton proportions, then wrapping up the full code output since the geometry is basically fully planned.
